input.prompt: Premium editorial photograph for a luxury health-technology brand campaign, not stock photography. The scene is set in a real, modern physical-medicine clinic fills the background: pale oak cabinetry, open shelves with folded towels and a few plants, a large window with soft daylight, contemporary medical equipment; shallow depth of field, so the room is softly blurred but clearly a real place, never a plain studio backdrop. Scene: the camera stands at the foot end of the treatment table looking along the patient's back toward her head, so her spine runs straight up the middle of the frame: the patient, a woman in her seventies with short silver hair, lies face down on a well-padded treatment table with a pillow under her chest and a light blanket over her hips and legs; the practitioner stands at the side of the table and holds a small chrome spring-loaded adjusting instrument shaped like a thick pen with a flat rubber tip (no needle) lightly against her mid back, his other hand resting still on her shoulder. Because the patient lies face down and the camera looks down at the back, the overlay is a BACK VIEW (posterior view) seen from above: the spine is a single straight column along the midline groove of the back, its row of spinous processes pointing up toward the skin and the camera, the vertebral bodies hidden beneath. Draw only the structures named, not the whole skeleton. Over the patient's body, a luminous augmented-reality anatomy overlay: the mid back only: a short straight column of vertebrae running up the middle of her back, with the inner ends of a few ribs on either side, drawn in delicate glowing teal engraving lines exactly where they sit under the skin, crisp and anatomically precise, like a living anatomical plate. The painful area glows with a soft, diffuse red-orange warmth inside the body at the mid back, subtle, like inflamed tissue seen through the skin, and the treatment is focused precisely on that red area. The overlay follows the body's real position and orientation: it lies inside the body exactly where those structures are for this pose (for a person lying down, the spine runs along the length of the body, horizontal in the frame), never pasted flat or upright across it. The practitioner is a man in a crisp white dress shirt with the sleeves rolled to the forearm and dark trousers, framed from the chest down so his head and face are out of the frame. The patient is a woman in her seventies with short silver hair, lying face down with a pillow under her chest and a bolster under her ankles; the patient's face may be seen, relaxed, eyes closed or looking away. Anatomy of the people: every hand has exactly five digits (one thumb and four fingers) with the thumb on the correct side for that left or right hand, is natural adult size in proportion to its body, and joins its own arm through a visible wrist. Every bare foot has exactly five toes and natural adult size. Each person has exactly two arms and two legs, all complete and joined to the body, in natural adult proportions. Every body is complete and continuous. No text, logos, labels or readable screens.
